 PLANNING 
Forward planning  
Variation No.1, No.2 & No. 3 to the County Development Plan 2021 - 2027  
Notice is hereby given that Laois County Council, in accordance with Section 58 of the Planning 
and Development Act 2024 and 2025 proposes to make variations (hereinafter referred to as 
"Proposed Variation No.1" or “Proposed Variation No.2”) to the Laois County Development Plan 
2021 – 2027 (hereafter referred to as ‘the Plan’). The Proposed Variation will be incorporated into 
Volume 1 and Volume 2 of the Plan as follows:  
 
Variation No.1 
The proposed variation to the Plan is intended to address specific, immediate policy updates that 
are needed in the short term and proposes that the following maps of the Portarlington Joint Local 
Area Plan (2025-2031) are included in the Laois County Development Plan (2021-2027): 
 
• 
Map 1 - Land Use Zoning 
• 
Map 2 - Objectives 
• 
Map 3 – Land Use Zoning, SAC and Flood Zoning 
• 
Map 4 – Green Infrastructure Adopted 
• 
Map 5 – Schematic Layout of Transport Elements 
 
and then include: 
• 
Mapping changes setting out proposed rezonings and the addition of residential zoned 
lands in response to the Ministerial Guidelines. 
 
Variation No.2 
The proposed variation to the Plan is intended to address specific, immediate policy updates that 
are needed in the short term and proposes to: 
 
• 
Include Map 12.1 (Land Use Zoning Map) and Map 12.2 (Objectives Map) of the Carlow 
Graiguecullen Joint Urban Local Area Plan (2024-2030) within the Laois County 
Development Plan 2021-2027, and then include: 
• 
Mapping changes setting out proposed rezonings and the addition of residential zoned 
lands in response to the Ministerial Guidelines. 
 
Public Consultation 
The proposed Variation No.1 and No.2 will be on public display from 25th February 2026 to 27th 
March 2026 (inclusive of both dates) where submissions will be accepted via http://consult.laois.ie; 
and in writing via the Planning Office, Laois County Council, Aras an Chontae, JFL Avenue, 
Portlaoise, Co. Laois. 
 
 
Variation No. 3  
This proposed variation to the Plan is intended to address specific, immediate policy 
updates that are needed in the short term and proposes the following: 
  
1. Amendments to the Volume 1 (Written Statement). 
2. Amendments to the Volume 2 (Settlement Strategy).

Local Enterprise Office 
LOCAL ENTERPRISE WEEK 2026 
 
Local Enterprise Week is organised and run by Local Enterprise Office Laois and is scheduled to 
take place from March 2nd to March 6th offering  a wide range of events and clinics that aim to 
celebrate and support local enterprise in County Laois. An initiative of the Local Enterprise 
Office, supported by Enterprise Ireland and Laois County Council, Local Enterprise Week offers 
many seminars, one to one mentoring clinics in person and online, most of which are free of 
charge. The clinics offer local businesspeople an opportunity to speak with experts to discuss 
key areas from financial skills, marketing to boosting their business online.  
 
 
 
Local Enterprise Showcase 2026  
 
Two Laois businesses took to the National and International stage as part of Local Enterprise 
Showcase 2026 which took place in the RDS Dublin from the 18th – 20th January 2026.  The 
first, Angelina George Skincare & MyComfort - Angelia George Skin is an award-winning natural 
skincare brand based in Portlaoise which was founded by having  a passion for sensitive and 
mature skin, blending nature-powered ingredients with advanced skin science to deliver real, 
visible results.   Secondly, MyComfort® which was launched in 2024 and founded in Portlaoise 
by Catherine Hearns, MyComfort® creates premium, sustainable sleep and migraine relief 
products.

Educational background, professional skills, and employment sectors

Poulastor Laois Premier at Dunamaise Arts Centre 
Laois County Council and Creative Ireland Short Film Bursary Awardees for 2024 
screened the Laois Premier of their film Poulastor to a full house at Dunamaise Arts 
Centre on Saturday 7th February 2026. 
 
Written by Cabrini Cahill and co-directed with AnnMarie Kelly and shot in County Laois, 
as an adaption of an earlier short story, dealing with end-of-life issues.  The film version 
Poulastor focuses John a middle-aged man (played by actor Charlie Hughes) who is 
receiving palliative care at home and follows his journey with Palliative Nurse (played by 
Sharon O’Brien).  Filmed across stunning Laois locations – including Kilone Hill, 
Abbeyleix, Ballykilcavan House, and the haunting Dunmore Caves – Poulastore is a 
tender meditation on connection at the end of life. 
 
The film received a very warm response from a full house audience at Dunamaise and 
was followed by a Q&A chaired by Producer Willie White (Business Development 
Manager ARISE TU Dublin).  The panel included: Director AnneMarie Kelly, Producer 
Mark de Carreau and Cinematographer Sean Weiss.  One audience member provided a 
really heartfelt response to the film, which she said helped her supported her grieving 
experience, highlighting the important role of professional palliative carers in supporting 
a loved one’s last journey.   
 
The production was selected by a panel led by acclaimed producer Arthur Lappin, The 
Boxer, Bloody Sunday & The Name of the Father and funded by Laois Arts Office & 
County Council in partnership with Creative Ireland, reflecting a strong 
commitment to nurturing original storytelling within the region.

theatre companies or artists to facilitate, manage and develop Laois Youth Theatre over 
the next three years 2026 – 2029. 
The successful applicant will manage, support and develop Laois Youth Theatre in 
Portlaoise and implement an annual Youth Theatre programme, with regard to the 
existing services and expertise within the Arts Service and supports provided.  During 
this pilot phase of development, the successful applicant will explore the potential for 
Laois Youth Theatre expansion into Portarlington.  The pilot phase will also scope out 
consolidation and resources to develop a more strategic approach for long-term Youth 
Theatre development in County Laois.  The provider will facilitate two Youth theatre 
groups during the school year, including an intensive summer camp/s to keep 
participants engaged and to encourage recruitment of new members. 
Laois Youth Theatre will be co-managed by the Laois Arts Office and the Dunamaise 
Arts Centre.  The Laois Youth Theatre is affiliated with Youth Theatre Ireland and is 
funded by Laois County Council and the Arts Council.

Ministerial Visit 
 
Laois County Council welcomed the Minister for Housing, Local Government and 
Heritage, James Browne TD on Friday 13th February 2026 for the official opening of 
five major housing developments delivered across the county.  A total of 164 new social 
and affordable homes were formally opened during the Minister’s visit, marking a 
significant milestone in Laois County Council’s ongoing housing delivery programme.   
 
The Minister visited the following developments;  
 
• 
Francis Dunne Court, Mountmellick – 49 homes 
• 
Harbour Court, Mountmellick – 6 homes 
• 
Carraig Glas, Stradbally – 26 homes 
• 
Rath Rua, Dublin Road, Portlaoise – 83 homes 
 
Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage, James Browne TD, said 
 
“Laois County Council genuinely stands out as a local authority that delivers when it comes 
to social housing. As Minister, I want to back ambitious councils, councillors and CEOs. What 
I am seeing from Laois is what I want to see more of elsewhere.  It’s important to recognise 
where things are being done. Year after year, Laois has surpassed their new-build targets, and 
notably, they had already exceeded last year’s target within the first nine months. This doesn’t 
mean we have enough housing built - there is still significant need and we want to do more. 
But it’s momentum and it’s a positive direction.  I want to see our local authorities cut through 
obstacles and focus on getting homes built.  The 164 new homes being opened today 
supported by my Department are clear proof of that commitment.  But let’s be clear. Beyond 
the figures and targets there are real people, individuals and families, who through a home 
gain the security of affordable, long-term housing.  This is the real, tangible impact of Laois 
County Council’s social housing programme.
